materials.item: PEX-b tubing, 1/2 inch (potable water supply)
materials.coverage: Sold in coils: 100 ft coil $31.10; 1,000 ft coil $230.95. low = 1,000 ft bulk rate, mid = 100 ft standard coil rate.
materials.source: SupplyHouse.com published online pricing (Bluefin PEX-b), captured 2026-07-27
materials.notes: High set equal to mid — no higher price point observed from this source. Widen once local supply house quotes land. Color (red/blue/white) does not affect price. NOTE: high may be understated — only the Bluefin house brand was captured for this diameter. The 3/4 inch data shows premium brands (Uponor PEX-a, Viega) running up to 2.8x the house brand on identical spec. Revisit this item's high value when capturing branded pricing.

materials.item: PEX-b tubing, 3/8 inch (fixture drops / short runs)
materials.source: SupplyHouse.com published online pricing (Bluefin PEX-b), captured 2026-07-27
materials.notes: Single published price point, no observed range. Note 3/8 inch prices HIGHER per foot than 1/2 inch — smaller specialty diameter, lower volume. Do not assume smaller pipe is cheaper. NOTE: high may be understated — only the Bluefin house brand was captured for this diameter. The 3/4 inch data shows premium brands (Uponor PEX-a, Viega) running up to 2.8x the house brand on identical spec. Revisit this item's high value when capturing branded pricing.

materials.item: PEX tubing, 3/4 inch (trunk / main supply lines)
materials.coverage: Sold in 100 ft coils. low = Bluefin PEX-b house brand $51.90/coil; mid = Uponor AquaPEX (PEX-a) $95.21/coil; high = Viega ViegaPEX $145.30/coil.
materials.source: SupplyHouse.com published online pricing (Bluefin / Uponor AquaPEX / Viega ViegaPEX), captured 2026-07-27
materials.notes: Range reflects BRAND TIER, not diameter — 2.8x spread on identical spec. Technical distinction behind the price gap: Bluefin is PEX-b (stiffer, crimp/clamp fittings); Uponor AquaPEX is PEX-a (more flexible, expansion fittings, different install method and tooling). These are genuinely different products, not just branding. Viega white $104.29 and red $128.87 also observed.

materials.item: Split system condenser (outdoor unit), 2-2.5 ton
materials.coverage: Outdoor condenser unit only — does NOT include indoor air handler.
materials.source: SupplyHouse.com published online pricing (Goodman / Comfort-Aire), captured 2026-07-27
materials.notes: Standard-efficiency Goodman GLXS3 line, 13.4 SEER2. CAUTION — DOE regional minimum efficiency standards split the US into North/South regions; Florida falls under the South region's higher minimum SEER2. Several units seen at this source were labeled 'North Region' and were EXCLUDED from this pricing as likely non-compliant for FL installs (their lower price reflects a lower compliance bar, not a better deal). If a North Region unit is ever the only data point for a given tonnage, flag it rather than using it as-is. These 2 and 2.5 ton units were labeled North Region at this source — no non-North-Region 2-2.5 ton alternative was found in this batch. USE WITH CAUTION, verify FL compliance before relying on this price point.

IMPORTANT SCOPE NOTE: RER issues permits ONLY for unincorporated Miami-Dade. All 34 incorporated municipalities run their own building departments and set their own fees — so county rows serve as the FALLBACK approximation for those cities, not their actual schedule, and any estimate using them should disclose that. Timeline not published in the fee schedule; a third-party permit expediter reports 1-10 business days for initial plan review, which is NOT an official county figure and was deliberately not recorded as timeline_days. Miramar and North Palm Beach checked but NOT added — only third-party sources found (permit expediters, contractor blogs), contradicting each other by 4x (5 to 21 business days) with no source claiming to quote the city's own stated policy. materials.item: PEX-b tubing, 1/2 inch (potable water supply)
materials.coverage: Sold in coils: 100 ft coil $31.10; 1,000 ft coil $230.95. low = 1,000 ft bulk rate, mid = 100 ft standard coil rate.
materials.source: SupplyHouse.com published online pricing (Bluefin PEX-b), captured 2026-07-27
materials.notes: High set equal to mid — no higher price point observed from this source. Widen once local supply house quotes land. Color (red/blue/white) does not affect price. NOTE: high may be understated — only the Bluefin house brand was captured for this diameter. The 3/4 inch data shows premium brands (Uponor PEX-a, Viega) running up to 2.8x the house brand on identical spec. Revisit this item's high value when capturing branded pricing.

materials.item: PEX-b tubing, 3/8 inch (fixture drops / short runs)
materials.source: SupplyHouse.com published online pricing (Bluefin PEX-b), captured 2026-07-27
materials.notes: Single published price point, no observed range. Note 3/8 inch prices HIGHER per foot than 1/2 inch — smaller specialty diameter, lower volume. Do not assume smaller pipe is cheaper. NOTE: high may be understated — only the Bluefin house brand was captured for this diameter. The 3/4 inch data shows premium brands (Uponor PEX-a, Viega) running up to 2.8x the house brand on identical spec. Revisit this item's high value when capturing branded pricing.

materials.item: PEX tubing, 3/4 inch (trunk / main supply lines)
materials.coverage: Sold in 100 ft coils. low = Bluefin PEX-b house brand $51.90/coil; mid = Uponor AquaPEX (PEX-a) $95.21/coil; high = Viega ViegaPEX $145.30/coil.
materials.source: SupplyHouse.com published online pricing (Bluefin / Uponor AquaPEX / Viega ViegaPEX), captured 2026-07-27
materials.notes: Range reflects BRAND TIER, not diameter — 2.8x spread on identical spec. Technical distinction behind the price gap: Bluefin is PEX-b (stiffer, crimp/clamp fittings); Uponor AquaPEX is PEX-a (more flexible, expansion fittings, different install method and tooling). These are genuinely different products, not just branding. Viega white $104.29 and red $128.87 also observed.

materials.item: Split system condenser (outdoor unit), 2-2.5 ton
materials.coverage: Outdoor condenser unit only — does NOT include indoor air handler.
materials.source: SupplyHouse.com published online pricing (Goodman / Comfort-Aire), captured 2026-07-27
materials.notes: Standard-efficiency Goodman GLXS3 line, 13.4 SEER2. CAUTION — DOE regional minimum efficiency standards split the US into North/South regions; Florida falls under the South region's higher minimum SEER2. Several units seen at this source were labeled 'North Region' and were EXCLUDED from this pricing as likely non-compliant for FL installs (their lower price reflects a lower compliance bar, not a better deal). If a North Region unit is ever the only data point for a given tonnage, flag it rather than using it as-is. These 2 and 2.5 ton units were labeled North Region at this source — no non-North-Region 2-2.5 ton alternative was found in this batch. USE WITH CAUTION, verify FL compliance before relying on this price point.

materials.item: Split system condenser (outdoor unit), 3 ton, heat pump
materials.coverage: Outdoor condenser unit only — does NOT include indoor air handler.
materials.source: SupplyHouse.com published online pricing (Goodman / Comfort-Aire), captured 2026-07-27
materials.notes: Goodman GLZS5BA3610, 16 SEER2 heat pump — high-efficiency tier, not North Region flagged. No straight-AC (non-heat-pump) 3 ton unit was captured in this batch for comparison; this price reflects heat pump tier specifically.

materials.item: Split system condenser (outdoor unit), 3.5-4 ton
materials.coverage: Outdoor condenser unit only — does NOT include indoor air handler.
materials.source: SupplyHouse.com published online pricing (Goodman / Comfort-Aire), captured 2026-07-27
materials.notes: 4 ton spread reflects EFFICIENCY/PRODUCT TIER, not size: low = Goodman GLXS4 straight AC 14.3 SEER2 ($2,719.70); mid = Goodman GLZS4 heat pump 14.3 SEER2 ($3,527.45); high = Goodman GLZS5 heat pump 16 SEER2 ($4,106.67). Comfort-Aire 3.5 ton AC ($3,681.38, R-454B refrigerant) falls within this range. A cheaper North Region 4-ton AC ($2,408.60) and a backordered Comfort-Aire 4-ton ($1,908.75, also flagged North Region-adjacent) were both excluded — see category caution note. Heat pump vs. straight AC is a real scope question to ask the client, not just a price tier.

flag: HVHZ NOTE: Palm Beach County is NOT in the High Velocity Hurricane Zone (FBC R202 defines HVHZ as Broward and Miami-Dade counties only). Palm Beach is Wind-Borne Debris Region — impact-rated products required, but not Miami-Dade NOA tier, which runs 30-50% higher. The three roofing material rows (architectural shingles, roof underlayment, ridge cap) copied from the Miami-Dade baseline carried HVHZ pricing and were REMOVED rather than left as overstated placeholders. Non-roofing materials (drywall, studs, tile, paint, pipe, concrete) are not HVHZ-sensitive and were retained. When materials expand to windows/doors/shutters, those MUST be split HVHZ vs non-HVHZ — that is where the 30-50% NOA premium actually applies. Broward retains the full Miami-Dade roofing copy correctly, since Broward IS HVHZ.
